title: Marquez / OpenLineage: emit a 2-job / 3-dataset run graph and read the downstream lineage back over TLS
description: 0.Q.1 (2026-07-21, ADR-0043) stands up the platform's OpenLineage backend -- a Marquez node (.127) fronted by nginx TLS (:443 -> api :5000, admin :5001, web :3000) at https://marquez.nexus.lab, backed by a dedicated PG17 HA pair (marquez-pg-1/2 @ .134/.135) with a keepalived VRRP VIP marquez-db.nexus.lab (.136) that Marquez reaches sslmode=verify-full. This demo does exactly what a real emitter (dataflow-studio, Prefect, Spark) does: the committed data-flow script POSTs OpenLineage run events describing a two-stage pipeline `raw.orders --[curate-orders]--> curated.orders --[load-dwh]--> dwh.fact_order`, each job as a START then a COMPLETE event (every POST returns 201), then reads the graph back through the REST read model -- the namespace, both jobs, all three datasets, and the lineage edges. This is the `if I change raw.orders, what downstream breaks?` view Marquez exists to answer, proven on live lab data rather than asserted. All probes are SSH-local-curl on the marquez node against its own CA (the Windows build host's schannel curl cannot validate the leaf by IP SAN). Namespace `nexus-lineage-demo`, kept distinct from the apply-time exit-gate namespace `nexus-lineage`. Cold-rebuild-proven 2026-07-21.

prerequisites.smokeGate: smoke-0.Q.1.ps1 ALL PASSED (reachability; docker-compose services up; Marquez API/admin/web + nginx TLS front door; PG streaming replication `streaming`; VIP .136 bound on exactly one pg node + TLS through the VIP with sslmode=verify-full; leaf SANs carry the VIP; an OpenLineage run-event round-trip). marquez node compose up, marquez-pg pair replicating.

observe.what: four OpenLineage POSTs each return 201 (curate-orders START+COMPLETE, load-dwh START+COMPLETE) into namespace `nexus-lineage-demo` at https://marquez.nexus.lab/api/v1/lineage; then the read-back lists 2 jobs (curate-orders, load-dwh) + 3 datasets (raw.orders, curated.orders, dwh.fact_order) + the downstream edges from raw.orders, and prints `Lineage graph verified`. This is a real emitter round-trip over the nginx TLS front door -- exactly what dataflow-studio/Prefect/Spark do.
the marquez api/web/nginx containers are Up while the events land -- the tier is serving OpenLineage ingest (:5000) behind the :443 terminator, not just running idle

an INDEPENDENT operator read of the read model: `GET /api/v1/lineage?nodeId=dataset:nexus-lineage-demo:raw.orders&depth=10` returns the full downstream graph -- raw.orders -> curate-orders -> curated.orders -> load-dwh -> dwh.fact_order. Traversing from the source dataset reaches the DWH fact through both jobs, proving the edges (not just the nodes) persisted.
the read model lists both jobs (curate-orders, load-dwh) in namespace `nexus-lineage-demo`, each with its input/output dataset facets -- the job-centric view of the same graph

steps.command: ssh -i $NEXUS_SSH_KEY nexusadmin@192.168.70.134 "sudo -u postgres psql -d marquez -c 'SELECT state, sync_state FROM pg_stat_replication'"

observe.what: marquez-pg-1 (.134, primary) shows its replica (.135) `streaming` -- the lineage graph the demo just emitted is committed to the dedicated PG17 pair and is being shipped to the standby. The backend HA is real, not decorative.

the keepalived VRRP VIP marquez-db.nexus.lab (.136) is held by exactly one pg node -- the address Marquez connects to sslmode=verify-full. A failover moves this VIP; the leaf SANs carry .136 so verify-full survives the move.

whatProves: The 0.Q.1 Marquez / OpenLineage tier receives lineage and answers downstream-impact queries end-to-end over its TLS front door: a real emitter round-trip POSTs a 2-job / 3-dataset run graph (`raw.orders --[curate-orders]--> curated.orders --[load-dwh]--> dwh.fact_order`, each START+COMPLETE, every POST 201) into namespace `nexus-lineage-demo` at https://marquez.nexus.lab/api/v1/lineage, and the read model returns the full graph -- both jobs, all three datasets, and the edges traversable from raw.orders via `/api/v1/lineage?nodeId=...&depth=10`. The lineage persists to a dedicated PG17 HA pair (marquez-pg-1/2) whose keepalived VIP marquez-db.nexus.lab (.136) Marquez reaches sslmode=verify-full, with streaming replication to the standby. Delivered as a cold-rebuild-proven tier (ADR-0043, 2026-07-21).
